maria (DevEx): FYI hitting a weird local-only 401 + retry loop when running the ruby sampleapp with a symlinked gem setup. figured i'd put notes here in case others hit it.

maria (DevEx): steps to repro: clone sampleapp, in the monorepo i do `bundle config local.redwood ../` and `bundle install`, then run `bundle exec ruby app.rb` and calls start failing after token refresh.

sam: curious — does it fail in CI too or only locally?

maria (DevEx): only locally for me. CI passes. logs show repeated 401 then retry and then eventual success after a full app restart. snippet:```
I, [2026-03-22T14:12:01.123Z]  INFO -- request: POST /v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
I, [2026-03-22T14:12:01.456Z]  INFO -- retrying request (attempt 1)
I, [2026-03-22T14:12:01.789Z]  INFO -- token refreshed, new token saved
I, [2026-03-22T14:12:02.012Z]  INFO -- request: POST /v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
```

devon: hmm. two quick guesses: 1) bundler local path symlink means you're loading the gem from the tree and possibly reusing a persistent Net::HTTP connection that still has the old token in memory; 2) the retry logic doesn't rewind some request state after refresh.

sam: +1 on connection reuse. ruby's Net::HTTP will reuse keep-alive sockets; if our code sets an Authorization header once when the connection is created, it might not update headers on subsequent requests over the same socket.

maria (DevEx): i did a quick hack: set `ENV['REDWOOD_DISABLE_KEEPALIVE'] = '1'` before the client init and the flaky 401s went away locally. not ideal but points to keep-alive.

devon: nice repro. could also try forcing `Connection: close` in the request as a test. either way, we should: 1) add a note to the sampleapp troubleshooting doc; 2) make token refresh update per-request headers rather than relying on connection-level state; 3) add a unit test that simulates token rotation + persistent connection.

sam: i'll open a tiny PR with the README note and the env var suggestion. can someone take the runtime fix? i can do the tests.

maria (DevEx): opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/pull/42 — includes doc note and a small example wrapper showing how to set `REDWOOD_DISABLE_KEEPALIVE=1` when running locally. cc @devon for server-side fix.

ci-bot: PR 42 — checks passed (unit, integration). :white_check_mark:

devon: thanks. i'll prototype a fix in the client that ensures Authorization header is set on each outgoing request object (not only at connection init). likely a one-line change in our http layer but need to run through test matrix.

maria (DevEx): great. can we add a short note in the devex docs about "why local symlinked gems + persistent connections can surface token refresh flakiness"? saves time for people doing local dev.

sam: added a new doc TODO in the repo under docs/dev-local.md in the PR. also left a small comment recommending adding a smoketest that runs sampleapp with local gem config in our dev matrix.

devon: will follow up w/ PR for client runtime fix, pinging eng-runtime if it affects other SDKs.

maria (DevEx): perfect — closing the loop here. thanks for quick triage. :sparkles: if anyone else hits this, drop me a note or reply here.

sam: thanks! :thumbsup:

ci-bot: merged PR 42 into main at 2001234788
